state: Choose the initial execution architecture for native Can tests. The user recommends existing Can execution plus generic native supervision. Can is written by AI agents; optimize reliable generation, explicit contracts, local repair and diagnostics, not human typing. Tests must allow arbitrary normal Can functions and keep scenarios, expectations, scheduling and report policy in Can; authored host harnesses must disappear. Native OS/driver operations may remain. Coverage, independent observations, bounded laptop load/disk and reliable cleanup are required. Backwards compatibility is unnecessary. This is documentation only: no builds, trials or measurements. Current Can emits TypeScript for Bun; checked IR exists but no general interpreter was found. A full interpreter must reproduce closures/identity, errors/occurrences, fixtures, coordination, resource ownership and all reachable platform behavior; it still needs process isolation and browser/DB/native bindings. Existing Go assertion supervision starts separate Bun processes with external deadlines, diagnostic bounds and generation leases, but its assertion protocol does not implement the requested live suite or complete process-tree/filesystem/remote-resource containment. All concrete functions require offline supplied assertions. Existing assert checks all source before optional root selection; focused live development may use a conservative verified dependency closure with all-root fallback and partial reports, while qualification requires all roots/cases/environments. The proposed topology is a generic Go outer supervisor, one Can controller, and Can case workers running a trusted suite artifact; Can owns discovery/selection/scheduling/verdicts. Native supervision only enforces limits, transports facts, reclaims resources and prevents success without completion/cleanup receipts. Candidate processes cannot inherit the private runner channel or supply trusted reports. No throughput evidence distinguishes fresh processes, pools or threads. Trust must identify a reference compiler/runtime/supervisor separately from the candidate compiler and candidate runtime. One option compiles the current suite once with an explicitly qualified reference toolchain, reconstructs its registry in workers and has the candidate compile only subjects. Missing reference APIs or syntax must stop or trigger a separate reviewed bootstrap refresh, not silently switch to the candidate. A replacement toolchain needs predecessor-compatible checks, independent fixed/negative controls and explicit qualification before promotion; there is no automatically self-proving first seed. Candidate ability to rebuild the runner is a separate output under test, not the authoritative judge. Alternative arrangements compile the suite with the candidate and compare controls, or use a frozen prebuilt suite with narrower source-update flexibility. Production emission/runtime/browser obligations always require the actual candidate artifacts even if a future interpreter runs the controller. Common parser/checker/runtime bugs can remain shared. Reuse builds within a run and retain compact provenance; do not keep default full private caches or disposable checkouts. Revisit an interpreter for a funded general-language need, meaningful semantic independence, or demonstrated backend overhead/observability limits after bounded improvements, not the mere presence of generated TypeScript.

backend.instructions: Which initial executor should this decision adopt under the supplied requirements and evidence?

criteria.existing_can: Use current Can TypeScript/Bun execution with generic native supervision, retaining full function semantics and specifying missing suite/platform contracts.
criteria.full_interpreter: Build a complete checked-IR interpreter now, including all required language/platform behavior and external supervision before calling migration complete.
criteria.new_codegen: Create a new native code-generation backend for the suite, with complete lowering/runtime support and generic supervision.

worker_boundary.instructions: Which initial case-isolation arrangement should be selected before any throughput measurements?

criteria.fresh_process: Use one fresh Bun OS process per case attempt/variant, with a separate controller and external ownership/deadline enforcement; accept startup cost and default to one active case.
criteria.process_pool: Keep a bounded pool of reusable Bun processes with specified state/resource reset verification between cases; amortize startup while adding cross-case contamination controls.
criteria.same_process_workers: Run cases in worker threads within a Bun process, define thread isolation and retain an external supervisor able to kill the whole container process on failure.

trust_relationship.instructions: Which trusted-runner relationship should govern authoritative candidate qualification?

criteria.reference_builds_suite: An explicitly qualified reference toolchain compiles the selected suite source; the candidate compiles subjects only. Block incompatible reference use, refresh separately and treat candidate runner rebuilds as additional subjects.
criteria.candidate_with_controls: Let the candidate compile the current suite and require independent control/reference comparisons before accepting its report; acknowledge that controls may miss self-miscompilation.
criteria.frozen_suite_artifact: Execute only an independently qualified frozen suite artifact; update its source and qualification separately, accepting limited immediate coverage of new test-source changes.
